l.i: Accipito hanc clemens animā, quam morte redemtam Ipse sua, propriam Christus sibi vendicat, hancq; Corporis ereptam vinclis, & carcere cæco Peccati & mortis, cælestem transfer in aulam, Inq; tuum nullo periturum tempore regnum, Hosq; meos anima postquàm seduxeris artus, Qui summo in terris, post te, Fridericus amore Est mihi dilectus, longos huic profer in annos Incolumem vitam, Satanæq; iniusta potenter Hunc odia atque minas contra defende feroces, Et mihi quam tanto donasti coniuge prolem, Hanc merito ornatam conserua semper honore, Ut videant læta seros in pace nepotes, Utq; Palatina æternùm stet gloria gentis. Quemq; tuos iuuenem Casimirum mittus in hostes, Huic animum & iustas in prælia suffice vires, Ut sæuo redeat confecta victor ab hoste Pace domum, & vera sit religionis asylum. Da, maneat Christi nostris ecclesia terris, Sinceroq; tuum nomen celebretur honore, Diuinoq; mei confirma flamine pectus Coniugis, in vasto quem gurgite linquo laborum, Ut tibi promeritos constans tueatur honores, Et populum sancta felix in pace gubernet.

page.notes: Printed letters with the superscript "q" abbreviations (hancq, Inq, Hosq, Utq, Quemq, Sinceroq, Diuinoq) are transcribed with their marks as seen; the reversed-C "Ↄ" forms are not present. The word "Palatina" and "vera" with a superscript mark are read as printed. Some letters in the italic verse are uncertain, notably "mittus" and "Satanæq", and "gurgite" and "linquo" are as printed. The FINIS line is set in spaced capitals and is treated as a closing word, not a heading.
